The one tenancy namespace that lives in core: ~*current-org*~ is the per-request thread-local the private addon binds, and this predicate is how core code asks ~am I the platform, or a tenant?~ without depending on the policy. Everything org-scoped downstream keys off this seam.

* 2. notify!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: platform/notify!
:FILE: src/graphden/tenancy/context.clj
:LINE: 176
:MINS: 1.2
:END:

The notification seam — the same install-a-hook shape as the capability predicates, pointed the other way: core RAISES a domain event (~:package-moderated~ with the decided row) and the addon decides who is told and how (the publishing org's owner, through the accounts Mailer, on the trusted origin). Without an addon the event is dropped, and the sink's result is never inspected — a mail failure is the sender's to log, not the domain write's to undo.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/tenancy/context.clj::(defn notify!][src/graphden/tenancy/context.clj:176]]

The SSRF egress guard a tenant's outbound call passes before dialing: fail-closed resolution of the hostname, rejecting loopback / RFC1918 / link-local / cloud-metadata targets. Pair it with ~validating-dns~ below in the same file — the connect-time re-check that closes the DNS-rebind TOCTOU.

* 6. sanitize-hiccup
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: platform/sanitize-hiccup
:FILE: src/graphden/web/hiccup_sanitize.clj
:LINE: 116
:MINS: 2.9
:END:

An allowlist walk over an EDN hiccup tree — permitted tags, permitted attrs, a depth cap and a node budget, returning nil for 'no representable output'. This is the gate on every path where GRAPH-authored markup reaches the editor's own DOM: typed value representations, component previews, server partials rendering user content. Anything not on the list collapses to escaped text rather than being rejected loudly — the sanitizer's job is to make the surface safe, not to argue with the author.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/web/hiccup_sanitize.clj::(defn sanitize-hiccup][src/graphden/web/hiccup_sanitize.clj:116]]
- see also :: [[file:crud.org::#crud/render-repr][render-repr]]

* 7. count!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: platform/count!
:FILE: src/graphden/util/counters.clj
:LINE: 65
:MINS: 1.2
:END:

Observability starts smaller than you expect: a process-global, monotonic ~{event → long}~ atom. Everything in docs/MONITORING.md — the usage rollups, the Prometheus scrape, the alerter's window below — is a diff of two ~snapshot~s of this map. Monotonic on purpose: readers diff rather than reset, so two of them can never invalidate each other's window.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/util/counters.clj::(defn count!][src/graphden/util/counters.clj:65]]

* 10. RemoteStorage
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: platform/RemoteStorage
:FILE: src/graphden/storage/remote/core.clj
:LINE: 112
:MINS: 3.8
:END:

The read side of BYO: a ~StorageCRUD~ leaf whose rows are an ATOM of ~{entity → [row …]}~ fetched from the hub over HTTP, with every write arm throwing ~read-only!~. The customer's executor compiles and runs the same graph while the hub stays the only writer — and ~refresh!~ swaps in a fresh bundle without rebuilding the record, which is what the SSE relay below triggers.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/storage/remote/core.clj::(defrecord RemoteStorage][src/graphden/storage/remote/core.clj:112]]
- see also :: [[file:storage.org::#storage/StorageCRUD][StorageCRUD]]

The customer-hosted executor assembly: RemoteStorage over HTTP as the read-only graph source, the SSE source for invalidation, and a direct http-server — the same core, assembled for someone else's hardware. Closes the platform block: the seams above are exactly what make this assembly possible.
